proposals.impact: convert 2 stalled sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: Two sessions landed on the quiz intro page in the last 48 hours. Neither started the quiz. The furthest_step_distribution shows both stopped at intro_load, meaning the intro screen itself is the wall. Both arrived via direct traffic, so these are warm visitors who typed or pasted the URL. They already decided to show up. Something on the intro screen stopped them before question one.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen's opening copy is almost certainly doing one of two things: making the quiz feel like a test they could fail, or describing what it is rather than what it costs them to ignore it. Joel's ICP (earners who don't build) already feel quietly ashamed of the gap between income and savings. If the intro reads like a diagnostic tool, they'll close it rather than risk confirmation. Replace the current intro headline and sub-copy with something that names the specific feeling of sitting with a good salary and still feeling financially stuck, using the specificity of Joel's own story (the gym-bag moment, the unopened tax-return tab) as the register. The call-to-action button label should also change from any generic "Start" phrasing to something that signals the quiz takes two minutes and reveals something they can actually use today.

proposals.impact: lift 66% open rate further and model best practice for lower-performing sequences
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% across 19 sends. Money Worship is lowest at 37.5% across 16 sends. The Vigilance sequence is outperforming the others by a meaningful margin, probably because "vigilance" speaks directly to the anxiety of watching money closely but never feeling safe. That tension is close to the surface for the ICP. The subject line in that sequence is most likely the cause. Looking at it now gives Joel a template to rewrite the Worship sequence's subject line, which would be the fastest lift available in email.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line from email-1 of the Money Vigilance sequence. Compare its register to email-1 of the Money Worship sequence. The Vigilance line is almost certainly more specific and more honest about a feeling, where the Worship line is probably more aspirational or achievement-framed. Rewrite the Worship email-1 subject line to match the Vigilance register: name the specific internal experience of someone who ties their self-worth to their account balance, without using any aspiration language. Do not promise a fix. Name the feeling. That is what gets opened.

proposals.impact: restore automated content publication and clear the 1-post queue backlog
proposals.observation: Two CI workflows failed on 4 July: "Daily Blog Post" at 06:28 and "Funnel-Hack Digest" at 10:43. The content queue shows one post waiting and no new publication since the three June posts listed. If the Daily Blog Post workflow is broken, that queued post is sitting unpublished and the automation that feeds the site's content cadence has silently stopped. With only one post queued, any further delay means a gap in the publication schedule that will affect organic reach and email triggers downstream.
proposals.proposal: Inspect the Daily Blog Post workflow run logs from 2026-07-04T06:28:35Z. The failure is most likely one of: an expired API token, a malformed frontmatter field in the queued post file, or a Node/dependency version mismatch introduced since the last successful run. The fix lives in the workflow YAML itself only if the cause is a runner or env-var issue. If the queued post's frontmatter is malformed, the fix lives in the post file. Either way, one file changes. Once the workflow passes, the queued post publishes and the cadence resumes. The Funnel-Hack Digest failure is a secondary concern and likely shares the same root cause, so fixing the blog workflow first will confirm whether they are linked.
